frequency_question: What proportion of major federal administrative rulemakings successfully complete all required procedural steps from initial notice to final publication in the Federal Register within a 279-day timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes all economically significant regulatory actions initiated by executive departments that require standard OIRA review, a formal public notice and comment period, and a published final rule. Excludes emergency interim final rules that bypass standard timelines.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named major rulemakings examined; all complex fee or major structural rulemakings failed to complete the full standard notice-and-comment cycle within a tight 279-day window due to the compounding durations of mandatory administrative steps.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical rulemakings that bypass OIRA significance thresholds.
skeleton: Standard federal rulemaking lifecycle phases: (1) Internal Agency Drafting & OIRA Preliminary Review (60-90 days), (2) Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Publication & Statutory Public Comment Period (60-90 days minimum, often 60 days), (3) Review of Comments and Draft Final Rule Preparation (60-120 days), (4) Final OIRA Review (30-90 days), (5) Publication and 30-to-60 day delayed effective date. Minimum theoretical physical time sum = ~240-390 days under optimal conditions.
multiplier: Sum of mandatory minimum statutory and administrative durations: 60 (drafting/OIRA) + 60 (comment) + 60 (analysis) + 30 (final OIRA) = 210 absolute minimum baseline days, easily expanding past 300-400 days for contested or high-fee structures.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act statutory requirements and standard OIRA review timelines remain legally fixed unless legislative reform occurs.
